items.title: Spring
items.text: Spring brings North Texas's heaviest thunderstorm activity to Plano, with heavy rainfall and occasional hail increasing the risk of roof leaks and flooding.

items.title: Summer
items.text: Summer storms and sudden downpours can still strain drainage systems, while high heat puts extra demand on aging water heaters and plumbing.

items.title: Fall
items.text: Fall weather in Plano can bring another round of storm systems, and falling leaves can clog gutters and downspouts, contributing to water intrusion around rooflines.

items.title: Winter
items.text: Occasional hard freezes in Plano can cause pipes to burst, especially in older homes, making winter a season to watch closely for sudden indoor water damage.

sections.heading: Water Damage Restoration FAQs for Plano Homeowners

items.q: How quickly should I call for water damage restoration in Plano?
items.a: You should call as soon as you notice standing water, leaks, or storm damage. The sooner restoration begins, the better the chances of limiting how far damage spreads through your property.

items.q: Will my homeowner's insurance cover the cost of water damage restoration?
items.a: Coverage depends on your specific policy and the cause of the damage. We can help document the damage thoroughly, but your insurance provider makes the final coverage decision.

items.q: Is it safe to walk through standing water in my home?
items.a: Standing water can hide electrical hazards or structural damage. It's best to avoid entering flooded areas, especially near outlets or appliances, and let trained professionals assess the situation safely.

items.q: What should I do if I smell sewage after flooding?
items.a: Avoid contact with the water and keep the area ventilated if possible, then contact a professional restoration team promptly rather than attempting to handle contaminated water yourself.
